relationships.subject: Insulin
relationships.evidence_quote: Insulin induced release of CGRP from meningeal afferents and consequent increases in dural blood flow through the activation of TRPV1 receptors of trigeminal afferents.

relationships.subject: Insulin
relationships.evidence_quote: Insulin sensitized both neural and vascular TRPV1 receptors making them more susceptible to the receptor agonist capsaicin.

relationships.subject: Capsazepine
relationships.evidence_quote: Preapplication of the TRPV1 receptor antagonist capsazepine reduced the CGRP-releasing effect of insulin (10 μM).

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: as a result of CGRP release from meningeal afferents, since pretreatment of the dura mater with the CGRP receptor antagonist CGRP8–37 abolished the vasodilator effect of insulin

relationships.subject: Insulin receptor
relationships.evidence_quote: Immunohistochemistry revealed colocalization of the insulin receptor with the TRPV1 receptor and CGRP in a significant proportion of trigeminal ganglion neurons.

key_findings: Insulin releases CGRP from trigeminal afferents via insulin receptor and TRPV1, raising dural blood flow
Insulin sensitizes neural and vascular TRPV1 to capsaicin; insulin receptor colocalizes with TRPV1 and CGRP in trigeminal neurons
